body: Confirmed. Looks like an issue in `node-ignore`. https://github.com/kaelzhang/node-ignore/issues/21

issue.title: Can't unignore pattern with **

repository.name: node-ignore
repository.description: 🔍 node-ignore is the manager and filter for .gitignore rules, the one used by eslint, prettier and many others.

issue.body:
This works:

``` js
const ignore = require('ignore')
var ig = ignore().add(['foo/*', '!foo/bar.js'])
ig.filter(['foo/bar.js'])
[ 'foo/bar.js' ]
```

This doesn't:

``` js
const ignore = require('ignore')
var ig = ignore().add(['foo/**', '!foo/bar.js'])
ig.filter(['foo/bar.js'])
[]
```

body: @jsnajdr reinstall eslint to upgrade `node-ignore` to `3.1.2` to see if it is ok now?

@kaelzhang The bug is only partially fixed with 3.1.2. With the following `.eslintignore`:

```
server/**
!server/a.js
!server/x/a.js
```

file `server/a.js` is not ignored any more, but `server/x/a.js` still is.

@jsnajdr Now that I think of it, for that to work, you would need to do:

```
server/**
!server/a.js
!server/x
!server/x/a.js
```

Does this work?
@alberto yes, this workaround works. But it shouldn't be needed - `!server/x/a.js` should just work.
@jsnajdr It's not a workaround. git works the same way
